lines.trans: Salma, wait—let me hold that wooden stool while you reach the top shelf!
I climb this little stool ten times a week, Nour, I just need the big teapot—ouch!
Salma! Grab my arm! Sit right down on this chair—don't stand up!
Ooh... my right shoe slipped on the bottom rung when I stepped down!
Let me slip your shoe off gently. Can you wiggle your toes for me?
Toes move fine, nothing broken—just a sharp twist on the outside of my ankle.
Keep your foot up on this second chair while I wrap cold ice in a clean towel.
No, no, Nour! Tomorrow is Wednesday! I have lentil soup and twenty lemon tarts to finish!
If you stand on a swollen ankle tonight, you won't walk for two weeks!
Who will bake Wednesday's fresh bread and lemon curd if I sit in a chair?!
Look around this house, Salma: you have six pairs of hands and one loud voice!
Wait... you want me to sit on a cushion and boss everyone around?!

meanings.note: Spontaneous Levantine exclamation when bumping or twisting something.

examples.text: آي! زحلقت رجلي عن طرف الطبلية!
examples.trans: Ouch! My foot slipped off the edge of the low stool!

examples.text: آي، إبريق الشاي لسا سخن كتير!
examples.trans: Ow, the teapot is still super hot!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أسابيع.

examples.trans: Next week I have time off.
We stayed at the guesthouse all week.

meanings.note: Plural أوامر means 'orders / instructions' (أوزع أوامر 'hand out orders').

examples.text: الشيف سلمى جاهزة توزع أوامر عالفريق كله!
examples.trans: Chef Salma is ready to issue orders to the whole team!

examples.text: تحت أمرك يا معلم، الشيش صار جاهز للتركيب.
examples.trans: At your service, boss—the shutters are ready to mount.

meanings.note: A sigh of dismay or tiredness, a little like English 'oof' or 'ugh'.

examples.trans: Oof, I forgot the key at home!
Ugh, it's hot today.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أباريق.

examples.trans: The teapot is hot on the table.
Pour the hot water into the teapot.

meanings.note: Everyday conditional word 'if' for real possibilities.

examples.text: رني الجرس إذا احتجتي أي شي.
examples.trans: Ring the bell if you need anything.

examples.text: إذا فتحنا الساحة الصبح، الجيران بيفرحوا.
examples.trans: If we open the courtyard in the morning, the neighbours will be delighted.

meanings.note: Everyday noun for a finger or toe; dual إصبعين ('two fingers'), broken plural أصابع.

examples.trans: Pull the paper out gently with two fingers.

examples.text: خلي أصابعك بعيدة عن الفرن السخن.
examples.trans: Keep your fingers away from the hot oven.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian pronoun 'you' when addressing one woman.

examples.trans: You must be Nour!
You are today's heroine, Nour.

meanings.note: Parts of the body in pairs are feminine in Arabic; 'my hands' is إيديي (iideyyi).

examples.trans: He washed his hands with warm water.
I planted the flowers with my own hand.

meanings.note: Command to a male to wait.

examples.trans: Wait a moment, I have an idea!
The suitcase is still waiting for its owner.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: The guest arrived Wednesday night.
We meet on Wednesday morning.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: باردة, plural: باردين).

examples.trans: Here, drink a glass of cold water.
My hands were cold from the rain.

meanings.note: Signature Levantine word for 'want / need', inflected with pronoun suffixes: بدي (I want), بدك (you want), بده (he/it wants), بدها (she/it wants), بدنا (we want), بدكم (you pl. want), بدهم (they want).

examples.trans: I want to read the booking ledger.
Jam bread needs unsalted butter.

meanings.note: Extremely common Jordanian word meaning both 'only / just' (بس نص كاسة 'just half a glass') and 'but' between clauses.

examples.text: بدي أقرأ الدفتر، بس مش ملاقي نظارتي!
examples.trans: I want to read the ledger, only I cannot find my glasses!
Just half a glass, please.

meanings.note: Everyday word for 'tomorrow' (بكرا الصبح 'tomorrow morning').

examples.text: بكرا الصبح رح نسبق المي الباردة!
examples.trans: Tomorrow morning we will beat the cold water!
We booked a quiet dinner — will you join us tomorrow?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: بيوت.

examples.trans: The old house has a lovely courtyard.
The neighbourhood houses are built of stone.

meanings.note: Preposition 'between, among'.

examples.trans: Today you are mending things between two brothers!
The table is between the window and the door.

meanings.note: Baked fruit or custard tart, especially تارت الليمون ('lemon tart').

examples.text: تارت الليمون بقشرة اللوز طلع أطيب واحد.
examples.trans: The lemon tart with the almond crust turned out to be the tastiest one.

examples.text: خلينا قطعة تارت صغيرة لطارق بالمطبخ.
examples.trans: We saved a small slice of tart for Tariq in the kitchen.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: تانية, plural: تانيين).

examples.trans: Room four is on the second floor.
There is a second sheet behind the letter.

meanings.note: Levantine relational adjective formed from تحت ('under/below') + -aani; opposite of فوقاني.

examples.trans: The tuning wrench is in the bottom drawer.

examples.text: نور مسحت الألواح التحتانية للشباك الكبير.
examples.trans: Nour wiped the lower panes of the tall window.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بتحرك, بيتحرك).

examples.text: في قطعة معدن تحركت جوا الصندوق!
examples.trans: A piece of metal shifted inside the box!
The car pulled away from the door.

meanings.note: Core Levantine verb for 'look (at)' taking على or في.

examples.text: تطلعي من الشباك شوفي لون الشيش الأخضر!
examples.trans: Look out the window and see the green colour of the shutters!

examples.text: ليش بتطلعوا علي هيك؟ هلا بمسح الدهان!
examples.trans: Why are you staring at me like that? I'll wipe the paint right now!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: تلوج.

examples.trans: The water is cold as ice.
Snow fell on the hills of Amman.

meanings.note: Used with right and left: الجهة اليمين 'the right side', من هاي الجهة 'from this side'.

examples.trans: The kitchen is on the other side.
Walk this way, it is closer.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أحذية.

examples.trans: Take off your shoes by the door.
Inside the bag are two pairs of men's shoes.

meanings.note: Transitive Form II verb ('move furniture, stir a pot, wiggle toes').

examples.text: حركنا البيانو خطوتين لورا بعيد عن الشباك.
examples.trans: We moved the piano two steps back away from the window.

examples.text: حركي الشوربة بملعقة خشب كل خمس دقايق.
examples.trans: Stir the soup with a wooden spoon every five minutes.

meanings.note: A very common preposition denoting physical surrounding or approximation of time/quantity.

examples.text: رتبنا الكراسي الخشب حوالين النافورة بالساحة.
examples.trans: We arranged the wooden chairs around the courtyard fountain.

examples.text: حط فوطة ناشفة حوالين قاعدة النبتة.
examples.trans: Place a dry cloth around the base of the plant.

meanings.note: Describes outer shutters, doors, or walls facing the courtyard or street.

examples.text: رح ندهن الشيش الخارجي بلون أخضر دافي.
examples.trans: We are going to paint the outside shutters a warm green.

examples.text: الباب الخارجي بيفتح مباشرة على شارع الياسمين.
examples.trans: The exterior gate opens straight onto Jasmine Street.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: خبزات.

examples.trans: The morning bread is fresh and hot.
We ate bread with cheese and olives.

meanings.note: Used for the material wood or timber.

examples.trans: The wooden ceiling is warm and quiet.
This is a hand-carved wooden train.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بخلص, بيخلص).

examples.trans: I finished making the bed quickly!

examples.text: كل ما أخلص عزف كنا نحكي.
examples.trans: Whenever I finished playing, we used to chat.

meanings.note: Very frequent Jordanian verb: خليني ('let me'), خلينا ('let us'), خليك ('stay!'), خلي ('keep/leave').

examples.trans: Let us open the door together.
Hot bread makes people pleasant!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بخبز, بيخبز).

examples.text: اخبزي قطع زوايا كتير يا سلمى!
examples.trans: Bake plenty of corner pieces, Salma!

examples.text: قديش بيقدر فرنك يخبز كل صبح؟
examples.trans: How much can your oven bake every morning?

meanings.note: Common everyday verb for 'went' in the past tense. Also used as a future particle.

examples.trans: We missed our chance — he hung up!

examples.text: كل التعب راح مع أول فنجان قهوة.
examples.trans: All the tiredness vanished with the first cup of coffee.

meanings.note: Feminine body-part noun in Levantine Arabic (رجلك اليمين 'your right foot').

examples.text: ارفعي رجلك عالمخدة وارتاحي نص ساعة.
examples.trans: Prop your foot up on the pillow and rest for half an hour.

examples.text: حطيت كيس تلج ملفوف بمنشفة على رجلي.
examples.trans: I placed an ice pack wrapped in a towel on my foot.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: رفوف.

examples.trans: The gold tin is on the top shelf.
There are two pieces left on the shelf.

meanings.note: Colloquial verb meaning to slip or slide, often accidentally.

examples.text: انتبهي عالدرج، الحجر لسا مبلول وبيزحلق.
examples.trans: Watch out on the stairs—the stone is still wet and slippery.

examples.text: زحلق كعبي عن الطبلية بس مسكت بالرخامة.
examples.trans: My heel slipped off the low stool, but I caught the counter.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أزواج.

examples.text: الزوجين دخلوا غرفة ستة قبل ساعة.
examples.trans: The couple checked into room six an hour ago.
They booked a quiet table for the couple.

meanings.note: The number 6.

examples.trans: Room six is on the second floor.
I have six lemons in the basket.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for 'to see, look, check' (بشوف / شاف).

examples.trans: Look inside the suitcase, Nour!
I will see you tomorrow at breakfast.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بشلح, بيشلح).

examples.trans: Take off your heavy coat and sit down.
He took off his wet shoes by the door.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: شوربات.

examples.trans: Here is a cup of hot vegetable soup.
Hot soup is wonderful on a rainy day.

meanings.note: Very common adverb in Jordanian Arabic for 'a little bit' or 'slowly'.

examples.trans: Wait a moment, I have an idea!
Turn the valve slowly and gently.

meanings.note: Adjective used for size (small) or age (young), masculine singular.

examples.trans: We found a little wooden train in the bag.
There are two small streets on the left.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أصوات.

examples.trans: I heard the sound of rain on the window.
His voice is calm and polite on the phone.

meanings.note: Used for fresh food, produce, or bread.

examples.text: خبز سلمى طازة وسخن كل صبح.
examples.trans: Salma's bread is fresh and hot every morning.

examples.text: اشترينا ليمون طازة ونعنع أخضر من السوق.
examples.trans: We bought fresh lemons and green mint from the market.

meanings.note: Everyday Levantine household word for a low wooden step-stool or small low table.

examples.text: طلعت عالطبلية الصغيرة عشان أوصل الرف العالي.
examples.trans: I stepped onto the low stool to reach the top shelf.

examples.text: حط الطبلية بالزاوية بعيد عن الممر.
examples.trans: Tuck the low stool into the corner out of the walkway.

طلع.gloss: to go up; go out; come out; turn out

meanings.en: to go up; go out; come out; turn out
meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بطلع, بيطلع).

examples.text: لفائف القرفة هلا طلعت من الفرن!
examples.trans: The cinnamon rolls just came out of the oven!
Go up the stairs to the third floor.

meanings.note: Names the horizontal rung of a chair/table or the upper crossbar of a frame.

examples.text: سندت رجلي عالعارضة التحتانية تبع الكرسي.
examples.trans: I rested my foot on the lower rung of the chair.

examples.text: علقنا الفانوس بوسط العارضة الخشب فوق القوس.
examples.trans: We hung the lantern from the middle of the wooden beam over the arch.

meanings.note: Can mean physically high or loud (for a voice or sound).

examples.trans: What is that loud sound upstairs?
The wooden ceiling is high and sunny.

meanings.note: Collective noun; شوربة عدس ('golden lentil soup' with lemon and olive oil) is a beloved Jordanian staple.

examples.text: شوربة العدس مع عصرة ليمون أطيب غدا بالشتا.
examples.trans: Lentil soup with a squeeze of lemon is the best lunch on a rainy day.

examples.text: سلمى غسلت العدس الأصفر وحطته عالنار.
examples.trans: Salma rinsed the yellow lentils and set them on the stove.

meanings.note: The standalone number ten.

examples.trans: You arrived ten minutes early.
Breakfast is from seven-thirty to ten.

meanings.note: The number twenty.

examples.trans: We need twenty eggs for breakfast.
The ring's width is twenty millimetres.

meanings.note: A very common preposition used to indicate location, possession, or presence.

examples.trans: A taxi just stopped at the door.
I have a reservation under the name Suad.

meanings.note: Adverb 'right away, at once'.

examples.trans: Count on me, I am heading out right away!
The hot water came back immediately.

meanings.note: Preposition for 'in' or 'at', and very commonly used to mean 'there is/are' (existential).

examples.trans: There is a small paper tag on the handle.
There is nobody standing in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Hollow verb meaning 'stand up / get up' (اوعي تقومي 'don't you dare get up!').

examples.text: خليكي قاعدة عالكرسي ولا تقومي أبدا.
examples.trans: Stay seated on the chair and don't get up at all.

examples.text: أبو طارق قام بكير وجهز إبريق الشاي.
examples.trans: Abu Tariq got up early and made a pot of tea.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بقدر, بيقدر).

examples.text: بنقدر نقدم زبدة مالحة مع المربى؟
examples.trans: Can we serve salted butter with jam?

examples.text: ليش ما قدرت تعطيه القطار بإيدك؟
examples.trans: Why could you not hand him the train yourself?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for soon or near.

examples.text: علمت بيانو ببيت قريب من هون.
examples.trans: I taught piano in a house near here.
We booked a table at a nearby restaurant.

meanings.note: Past tense verb meaning to sit down, or sometimes to stay/remain in a place.

examples.trans: Please have a seat in the courtyard under the tree.

examples.text: ضيفة غرفة أربعة رح تقعد كل الأسبوع.
examples.trans: Room four's guest will stay the whole week.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian plural is قوايا (qawaaya): كرسيين قوايا ('two sturdy chairs').

examples.trans: The gate rang with one strong ring.
We brought two sturdy wooden chairs to the courtyard.

meanings.note: Anatomical and everyday word for 'ankle' (كاحلي اليمين 'my right ankle').

examples.text: الحمد لله كاحلي مش وارم، بس بده راحة.
examples.trans: Thankfully my ankle isn't swollen—it just needs rest.

examples.text: حطينا تلج عالكاحل ربع ساعة وخف الوجع.
examples.trans: We put ice on the ankle for fifteen minutes and the ache eased.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: كبيرة, plural: كبار).

examples.trans: We use this big paper ledger.
You know older brothers well!

meanings.note: An everyday item of furniture for sitting.

examples.trans: We placed eight chairs around the tables.
I tightened the screw on the wooden chair.

meanings.note: Culinary noun used for كريمة الليمون ('lemon curd / cream') and pastry fillings.

examples.text: نور جهزت كريمة الليمون الصفرا للتارت.
examples.trans: Nour prepared the bright yellow lemon curd for the tarts.

examples.text: ريحة كريمة الليمون الطازة عبت المطبخ كله.
examples.trans: The aroma of fresh lemon curd filled the entire kitchen.

meanings.note: A highly versatile quantifier used to mean 'all of', 'every', or 'the whole'.

examples.trans: Tell me everything I need to know.
Everyone is happy in the courtyard today.

meanings.note: Vocalized with fatha-sukun to distinguish noun كَسْر ('fracture') from verb كسر ('to break').

examples.text: طمنونا، ما في أي كسر بالرجل الحمد لله.
examples.trans: Good news—there is no fracture in the foot, thank goodness.

examples.text: اللوية الخفيفة بتطيب بسرعة لما ما يكون فيها كسر.
examples.trans: A mild sprain heals quickly when there's no fracture.

meanings.note: Attached prefix ل- before nouns ('for/to'); before pronoun suffixes in spoken Jordanian it takes the stem إل-: إلي ('for me / mine'), إلك ('for you / yours'), إله ('his'), إلها ('hers'), إلنا ('ours'), إلكم ('yours pl.').

examples.trans: The blue suitcase is mine.
Thank you all very much!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for 'no' or 'not', used exactly like Standard Arabic.

examples.trans: No, lift the handle first.
Do not worry, ma'am.

meanings.note: Invariant modal word followed by a subjunctive verb (without ب-) to express 'must / have to / need to'.

examples.trans: Tell me everything I need to know.
Everything has to be just right!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بلف, بيلف).

examples.text: لفي شمال برا البوابة وامشي دغري.
examples.trans: Turn left outside the gate and walk straight.
Turn left at the stair landing.

meanings.note: Common conjunction used to introduce a time clause, distinct from the question word 'when' (mita).

examples.trans: Smile when the bell rings!
When I get nervous, my sentences turn long.

meanings.note: Instance noun from لوى ('twist/turn'): لوية خفيفة = 'a minor twist/sprain'.

examples.text: هي بس لوية خفيفة بالكاحل وبكرا بتكون أحسن.
examples.trans: It's just a minor twist in the ankle and tomorrow it'll feel better.

examples.text: الراحة والتلج أحسن دوا للوية الكاحل.
examples.trans: Rest and ice are the best remedy for an ankle twist.

meanings.note: Definite الليلة means 'tonight', while indefinite ليلة means 'one night / night of'.

examples.trans: I am going to sleep well tonight.
We booked the room for three nights.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: ليمون.

examples.trans: The warm lemon cake is ready.
I squeezed half a lemon into the soup.

meanings.note: Used mostly as a negative particle for verbs ('didn't') or as a relative pronoun/conjunction ('what' or 'that which').

examples.trans: Paper does not lose room names.
Have tea before you head out.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: مخدات.

examples.trans: I put two soft pillows on the bed.
The cotton pillow is comfortable for sleeping.

meanings.note: 'Marrah' means 'a time/once' (e.g. waḥdeh marrah = one time), but 'mara' (مَرَة) means 'woman/wife' in colloquial Jordanian.

examples.trans: The doorbell rang twice.
I read the letter three times.

meanings.note: Passive participle of رفع ('lift/raise').

examples.text: خلي رجلك مرفوعة عالمخدة طول السهرة.
examples.trans: Keep your foot propped up on the pillow all evening.

examples.text: راسك مرفوع يا طارق، خبزاتك بطيروا العقل!
examples.trans: Hold your head high, Tariq—your loaves are amazing!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بمسك, بيمسك).

examples.trans: Hold this torch steady right here.
Grab the boxes, Tariq!

meanings.note: Common defective verb for walking on foot or things running smoothly.

examples.text: ممنوع تمشي عكاحلك لحد بكرا الصبح.
examples.trans: You mustn't walk on your ankle until tomorrow morning.

examples.text: مشينا عالهدا بالساحة بعد ما وقفت المطر.
examples.trans: We walked gently across the courtyard after the rain stopped.

meanings.note: One of the most basic Arabic prepositions indicating origin.

examples.trans: I am Salma from the kitchen.
Breakfast is from seven-thirty to ten.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: مناشف.

examples.trans: The room has clean white towels.
Here is a dry towel after the rain.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for 'good' and adverbially 'well' (نمت منيح؟ 'did you sleep well?').

examples.trans: It has a good, comfortable wooden bed.
Did you sleep well under the wooden ceiling?

meanings.note: Interrogative pronoun used for people.

examples.trans: Who left this envelope here?
Whose is this brown leather notebook?

meanings.note: Natural spoken Levantine pronunciation of نظيف ('clean'), broken plural نضاف.

examples.text: مسحنا الفرشاية بقماشة نضيفة ومي دافية.
examples.trans: We wiped the brush with a clean cloth and warm water.

examples.text: المطبخ صار نضيف ومرتب وجاهز لبكرا الصبح.
examples.trans: The kitchen is spotless, tidy, and ready for tomorrow morning.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بنزل, بينزل).

examples.trans: The guests will come down at half past seven.
I came down to ask about the sink water.

meanings.note: Cardinal number or used as an indefinite pronoun.

examples.trans: Not a single scratch on the cup!
The gate rang with one strong ring.

meanings.note: Active participle of ورم ('swell up').

examples.text: كويس إن كاحلك مش وارم، التلج فاد علطول.
examples.trans: It's good that your ankle isn't swollen—the ice helped right away.

examples.text: إذا ضلت الرجل وارمة الصبح منروح عالدكتور.
examples.trans: If the foot is still swollen in the morning, we'll see the doctor.

meanings.note: Form II verb for distributing flyers, portions, or kitchen tasks.

examples.text: سلمى قعدت عالكرسي ووزعت الشغل عالكل.
examples.trans: Salma sat in the chair and assigned tasks to everyone.

examples.text: نور وزعت كروت الدعوة عجيران الحارة.
examples.trans: Nour handed out invitation cards to the neighbourhood.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بوقف, بيوقف).

examples.trans: A yellow taxi stopped outside the gate!
My heart stopped at page one!

meanings.note: Vocative particle used when addressing someone directly.

examples.trans: Good morning, Tariq!
Oh, how lovely the sun is after the rain!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: The green pharmacy is on your right.
We hung the board to the right of the desk.
